Header: 2026-09-16 10:00 PT | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Rajesh Mehta (CTO - Nimbus), Lina Gomez (Lead ML Eng - Nimbus), Tom Alvarez (Head of Security - Nimbus), Priya Rao (DevOps - Nimbus)

Auto-generated Summary: weekly poc check-in, onboarding progress, env readiness, actions captured.

00:00:02 Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, uh this is Alex from Redwood, we've got Samira and Miguel with me, um quick agenda — access & infra status, bench results, tuning notes, security asks, next steps.
00:00:18 Rajesh Mehta: yep thanks Alex, I'll be brief, we're pretty excited to see the latency numbers start to settle, we had some trouble with the VPC peering config last week so i want to confirm that's resolved.
00:00:35 Samira Patel: cool, on our side we saw the peering handshake succeed but a few routes were missing — Priya, did you push the NAT rules?
00:00:44 Priya Rao: yes i pushed them yesterday but i think one of the subnets was a /24 mismatch so a couple of GPUs couldn't talk to the logging endpoint, that's fixed now, i also opened tcp 443 to the control plane.
00:00:57 Miguel Torres: small note: when we did the bench we got intermittent 95th percentile spikes to ~420ms, but median was around 110ms on the model shard we used (gpt-3 style open model).
00:01:12 Lina Gomez: right and just to clarify, our production target is 200ms p95 for user-facing queries, so those spikes are a concern.
00:01:25 Samira Patel: understood — quick context: the pilot infra is using 2xA100s with a mix of CPU box for batching; KV cache is enabled but we haven't tuned the prefix cache TTLs, that often accounts for the p95 spikes if cache misses happen.
00:01:43 Tom Alvarez: can you spell KV cache again? sometimes our security doc has it as "KV-cache" and i want to match the naming. Also, where are logs stored, and is KMS used for key rotation?
00:01:56 Alex Kim: good q — we call it KV cache (sometimes hyphenated in older docs), logs go to your VPC logging endpoint or to Redwood-managed S3 (opt-in), and yes we support customer-managed keys via KMS / HSM integration. we'll send the KMS detail in the security pack.
00:02:15 Rajesh Mehta: nice. About the bench runs — can you remind me which model variant you used and whether quantization was on?
00:02:25 Samira Patel: variant was redwood-open-7b-quant (note: internal name), we ran int8 quant on the model for cost reasons; results were with batching size 8 and batching latency window at 20ms.
00:02:40 Lina Gomez: that could explain the spikes, quantization sometimes adds jitter on tail latency depending on kernel selection. Did you run with the model in single-GPU KV cache mode or multi-shard?
00:02:52 Miguel Torres: single shard for this run; multi-shard introduces KV cache warmup times and networking overhead, which we expect to look at next week.
00:03:06 Alex Kim: ok let's walk through the onboarding checklist quickly — access: Redwood has org-level SAML SSO set up for Lina, Rajesh, and Tom?
00:03:16 Tom Alvarez: SSO is set up, we tested login, but api-key rotation needs to be scoped — our policy is 30 days rotation, is that supported?
00:03:27 Alex Kim: yes we support rotation and short-lived tokens with the private control plane; for hosted we can rotate keys via the console or API. we'll include rotation examples.
00:03:39 Priya Rao: on the networking side, we still need to confirm CIDR ranges for the peering. I ran a traceroute and saw a couple of timeouts earlier which matched the bench spike times.
00:03:52 Samira Patel: ok, for the bench itself we suggested two flows: 1) synthetic latency bench to measure p50/p95/p99; 2) real prompt set of ~2k transcripts for quality and regression. Lina, you said you'd upload the artifacts?
00:04:06 Lina Gomez: yes i've uploaded an initial 500 transcripts to the shared drive under /docs/poc/nimbus/benchmarks — i'll add the rest by Friday.
00:04:18 Alex Kim: perfect. On tuning: quick levers we discussed — increase KV cache TTL for stable prefixes, aggressive batching for background jobs, lowering batching window for UI flows, and consider a different kernel/quant profile if p95 is still high.
00:04:34 Miguel Torres: and we should test with prefix caching pre-warm; the first N requests are cold and can cause spikes so we need warmed caches for the 99th.
00:04:46 Rajesh Mehta: can Redwood run a warmup script as part of the bench harness?
00:04:50 Samira Patel: yep we can include a warmup phase — we'll run 10k short requests to populate KV and prefix caches before the timed run.
00:04:59 Tom Alvarez: security: we need audit logs, retention 12 months, and RBAC for developer vs ops roles. Can Redwood restrict Console access by IP?
00:05:11 Alex Kim: yes RBAC is supported — roles can be scoped, and console access can be restricted via IP allowlist when using Private deployment; for hosted we can restrict via SAML group mappings and session policies.
00:05:27 Tom Alvarez: Great — also need to confirm encryption in transit for inter-shard comms.
00:05:33 Miguel Torres: inter-shard uses mTLS in our runtime, and you can require customer-managed keys on disk via KMS for the private infra. we'll put the architecture diagram in the pack.
00:05:45 Rajesh Mehta: on pricing — we discussed Dedicated vs Hosted earlier. For this pilot, are we still on hosted consumption?
00:05:53 Alex Kim: yes this POC is hosted but we've provisioned a dedicated pool for the pilot so you get predictable throughput; if you move to Dedicated reserved it's a different contract but similar infra.
00:06:06 Lina Gomez: one more quick note — we'd like to run a regression test of model quality after quant changes; how do you recommend we track regressions?
00:06:15 Samira Patel: we can tie quality regressions into Redwood Optimize evaluations — we can run the sample prompts and surface a delta report. we'll include the eval harness and threshold examples.
00:06:27 Priya Rao: on ops, what's the best way to send logs to our SIEM? syslog? s3?
00:06:34 Alex Kim: both options — you can stream logs to your SIEM via our logging endpoint or forward from S3. we'll include sample config.
00:06:44 Rajesh Mehta: ok let's capture concrete next steps — Samira will run the bench, we'll get the remaining transcripts uploaded, Alex sends security pack, Nimbus to finalize VPC details.
00:06:58 Alex Kim: exactly, and Samira will also try a non-quant run (fp16) to compare tail latency.
00:07:08 Samira Patel: yep plan is: run quantized int8 run, then fp16 run, both with cache warmup, and attach logs to the bench spreadsheet.
00:07:18 Lina Gomez: what about cost numbers? can you share estimated tokens/second cost for the current pilot config?
00:07:26 Alex Kim: we'll put cost per 1k tokens for the pilot in the follow-up; rough ballpark is in the benchmark sheet but we'll formalize it.
00:07:35 Tom Alvarez: small transcription glitch i noticed in earlier notes — the product name got logged as "Redwood Dedicate" instead of 'Dedicated' — just FYI.
00:07:44 Miguel Torres: ha yeah the auto-transcript is messy sometimes.
00:07:48 Rajesh Mehta: any blockers on your side?
00:07:51 Samira Patel: main blocker was the VPC route/mismatch which Priya fixed; other than that we need the rest of transcripts and the ip ranges, and we need to get approval for the security deep-dive date.
00:08:04 Priya Rao: we'll aim to get IPs and NAT config by Monday.
00:08:09 Alex Kim: awesome — we'll follow up with meeting notes and the pack. Is everyone ok for a quick 30m security call next Thurs? (2026-09-24)
00:08:20 Tom Alvarez: yes that's fine.
00:08:22 Lina Gomez: works for me.
00:08:24 Rajesh Mehta: fine.
00:08:26 Alex Kim: great — last thing: shared artifacts i mentioned: link to bench sheet: https://redwood.share/bench/nimbus-2026 and security pack (will send via secure link).
00:08:41 Samira Patel: action items repeated in the notes and i'll post the bench results to the sheet and slack channel.
00:08:48 Alex Kim: thanks all, we'll reconvene next week same time, call closed.

Auto-generated Action Items (end): Samira to run bench and warmup, Alex to send security docs, Nimbus to provide network and datasets.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps and product name typos (e.g., Redwood Dedicate), timestamps approximate, speaker labels mostly accurate.
